Definition: from G3756 and G4452; not yet:--hitherto not, (no…) as yet, not yet.
BiblicalUsage: This is the word of what is coming. Paul fed the Corinthians with milk and not with meat, for hitherto ye were not able to bear it, and John says it doth not yet appear what we shall be, but when He shall appear we shall be like Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe not yet is the word of growing up: I was fed with milk because I was not yet able to bear meat, and it does not yet appear what I shall be.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
